newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Oct inflation 4.2 pct vs 4.5 pct yr-ago.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Oct inflation 4.2 pct vs 4.5 pct yr-ago.

text.p: Venezuela's inflation rate was 4.2 percent in October, down from 4.5 percent in October 1995 and up from 3.6 percent in September this year, the Central Bank said.
October's rate brought inflation over the past 12 months to 114.4 percent, compared to 51.1 in the year to October 1995, the bank said.

It was the fifth consecutive drop in the monthly rate since a peak of 12.6 percent in May, an immediate consequence of the launch in April of an IMF-supported economic reform program. The plan freed currency and interest rates and increased gasoline prices fivefold.
Cumulative inflation for the first 10 months of the year now stands at 91.5 percent, compared to 39.9 percent for the same period of 1995.

Government officials, confident that the worst of the inflationary impact had now passed, have predicted that inflation rates would fall to about two percent at the end of the year, in line with IMF targets.
Inflation for 1996 will be 95 percent, compared to 56.6 percent in 1995, they have said. It is seen falling to around 35 percent in 1997.

Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar, stressing that "underlying inflation is broken", said last week he expected an October "blip" essentially because of a rise in electric rates by an average 50 percent on October 4.
The Central Bank, in a statement, attributed the October inflation rate mainly to increases in electricity, water and public transport (metro) rates.

"These adjustments ... had an indirect impact on all goods, in particular food, drinks and tobacco," it said. Without the direct effect of the rises in these basic services, "the inflation rate would have been 3.1 percent."
"Household expenditures" was the category which registered the highest price rise in October, up 5.9 percent, compared to 3.2 percent in September.
